Edgar was a highly ranked junior in Mexico and played for the University of Texas, where he completed an undergraduate degree in business and a graduate degree in exercise physiology. Starting as an assistant coach in his alma mater, Edgar has been coaching high performance players for the last 25 years. He's a national coach for the USA, Germany and Mexico. He's been a speaker at many national and international coaches conventions and as a partner with TennisGate, a player development media company. Edgar directs the tennis program at the Norfolk Country Club in Connecticut. He's a member of the ITF Coaches Commission and today he's here to talk to us about some of the key ways to improve your players. Welcome Edgar. Hello everyone, Edgar Giffening here. I'm going to talk to you about pretty obvious topic, helping your players improve. It sounds quite obvious, but I think as coaches, sometimes we kind of forget that the main reason, our main objective for being a tennis coach is helping players improve, making players better. After 50 years of coaching tennis, you kind of realize that a lot of players don't really improve. They play a lot, but they always stay at the same level and it is our job as coaches to help them get better. I think better players get motivated, really striving to improve your game. It's a huge motivation for everyone
